CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left arm pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports left arm pain beginning approximately two weeks ago. He woke at around 2 AM with severe pain and applied ice for relief. He sat on the side of the bed holding his arm down in an attempt to improve circulation, but this did not help. The pain eased around 4-5 AM and he returned to sleep. This pattern of nighttime pain with daytime residual symptoms the following day repeated over several nights. The pain originates in the hand and radiates down the entire arm. Patient denies that neck movement or head turning exacerbates arm pain and denies shoulder discomfort with movement. He reports weakness in his hand, particularly with gripping. He has a previous finger injury that does not function properly. He was evaluated by another physician who diagnosed a pinched nerve and prescribed numbing medicine, a neck pill, and gabapentin. Since starting these medications, nighttime symptoms have significantly improved. Most recently, his neck has not been bothering him for the past couple of nights, though his hand continues to be symptomatic.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Veteran with 1% disability rating. Peripheral neuropathy affecting lower extremities from knees to feet. Cervical arthritis with disc degeneration.

MEDICATIONS
Numbing medicine
Neck pill
Gabapentin (dosage uncertain; patient unsure if taking 300 mg or 100 mg)
Eliquis

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a Veteran. He has a lady friend who assists him with medication management. He presents in a wheelchair.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Elderly white male presenting in wheelchair, no apparent distress. Cervical spine: non-tender, mildly restricted cervical extension with symmetric right and left lateral rotation causing mild lateral neck pain but without radicular pain. Spurling's maneuver benign. Neurologic: 1+ bilateral biceps, triceps, and brachioradialis reflexes. Upper extremity strength: bilateral hand grip strong. Sensation: symmetric in both hands. Gait not assessed today. Lower extremities and other findings examined per template.

RESULTS
Cervical X-ray: reveals significant disc degeneration at C5-6 and to a lesser extent at C4-5 and C3-4. Significant lower lumbar facet arthropathy at C6-7. C7-T1 difficult to visualize on current x-rays. Cervical MRI: ordered, pending.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Left upper extremity neuropathy suspicious for cervical radiculopathy, with possible contribution of peripheral neuropathy
2. Neck pain in the setting of cervical arthritis and disc degeneration

Suspect this is a flare of cervical radiculopathy. Continue current medications including gabapentin twice daily and home exercise program. Cervical MRI ordered to determine exact location of nerve root compression. Tentatively plan left C7-T1 epidural injection with exact location to be determined based on MRI results. Patient denies blood thinners. Follow up after MRI and epidural injection to assess degree of symptom relief.
